models.headline: Mistral Large 4 is a new open-weight model you can try through a preview API now
models.summary: Mistral's new model has 1 trillion parameters, and its public preview is live today while the downloadable weights arrive later this month.
models.why_it_matters: You can test it through Mistral's preview API now, and the weights are promised for the end of the month, so you can run it yourself.
models.for_builders: Open the preview API on Mistral Studio and test coding or document tasks.

extra.source_text: Le chonk Introducing Mistral Large 4 Back to Blog 14 min read October 6, 2026 By Mistral Share this post Copy url to clipboard Copied Le Chonk Today, we’re launching a public preview of Mistral Large 4. Unofficially ML4, very officially: le Chonk . ML4 pushes the frontier of open-weight performance. You can try the preview API today on Mistral Studio . Weights drop end of this month. Frontier performance ML4 is a 1 trillion-parameter natively multimodal model with 52 billion active parameters. It is our largest and most capable model to date, and it continues to improve rapidly as we refine it. The model demonstrates exceptional performance across coding, agentic workflows, and multimodal understanding. It already achieves performance competitive with the strongest open-source models globally, while significantly outperforming any open-weight model developed in the US or Europe. On critical enterprise workloads, including cybersecurity, finance and law, we find it to be state-of-the-art among open models. In some domains such as visual grounding, it goes further still, surpassing even frontier closed models. We will release the weights by the end of the month. Until then, we are red-teaming the model in real-world settings with cybersecurity leaders, vetted partners, and state authorities, who will access the same model with reduced moderation and expanded cyber capabilities. Coding - DeepSWE Coding - Terminal Bench 4.0 Cyber Agentic behaviour Finance Agent Harvey's Legal Agent Grounding Forged in Europe. Built for AI sovereignty. ML4 was trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral’s own datacenters in Europe. The public preview is served on that same infrastructure. It is a significant milestone in our long-term investment across infrastructure, research, and product development: state-of-the-art performance in critical verticals, delivered through open weights, designed to give customers control over their AI. This is particularly important in cybersecurity, where provider-level refusals can block legitimate vulnerability research and incident response, and where losing access to a capability mid-incident can itself become a critical security risk. ML4 pairs top-tier cyber performance with open weights and self-deployment, giving organizations both the capability and the autonomy to run advanced security work under their own policies. The model will be available across multiple regions worldwide, including a European deployment that Mistral operates end-to-end, independently of other digital service providers and under European law. Fun fact: a significant share of ML4’s training data was multilingual, spanning more than 160 languages, including every official language of the European Union. We’ve been working closely with leading enterprises across the world in finance, engineering, manufacturing, logistics, pharmaceuticals, science, shipping, public sector, and other mission-critical industries to train ML4. In fact, the model uses the same training, customization, and RL environment we offer our customers through Mistral Forge. Try it today There is still more to come. As we work toward releasing the weights, we will share further details on the model architecture, additional benchmarks, and our post-training methodology. This model will also serve as the foundation for a new generation of specialized and optimized Mistral models. In the meantime, we invite you to try the preview API and share your feedback with us on social media. Capabilities deep-dive Cybersecurity ML4 is one of the world's strongest AI models for cybersecurity. On the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index, an independent evaluation of how well AI models find and fix security flaws in real software, it ranks among the top five models globally and leads open-weight models developed outside China by a wide margin. On one of the index's tests, which asks a model to reproduce a real vulnerability in open-source software and then patch it, ML4 scores 82%, the highest of any model. It also solves 93% of the challenges in Cybench, a set of 40 exercises drawn from security competitions, one of the highest scores reported for an open-weight model. That top score reflects a practical advantage. Several leading closed models, including Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, score near zero on the same test because they refuse to perform the task. Yet defending software often starts with proving that a flaw is real, exactly the kind of work safety filters in closed models can block. This matters even more as threat actors increasingly jailbreak those same models to support offensive cyber activity: defenders need systems that can match those capabilities without being constrained by the same refusals. ML4 can do that work, and its capabilities extend beyond what it was explicitly trained for: in internal testing, it proved useful for analysing malware, prioritising vulnerabilities, and writing detection rules. For organisations that need sovereign, auditable AI for security operations, it will be able to run on private cloud or on-premise. ML4 against the field : efficiently reasoning over diverse complex challenges Malware reverse-engineering: solving an out-of-distribution investigation task AA Cyber Index CyberGym-E2E Cybench Agentic coding ML4 excels across software engineering, repository understanding, and complex terminal workflows, scoring 61.7% on DeepSWE v1.1, 59.4% on SWE-Atlas-QnA, and 28.3% on Terminal-Bench 4. Its combined Coding Agent Index score of 49.8% places it ahead of DeepSeek V4 Pro 0813 and Qwen3.8 Max. DeepSWE 1.1 Terminal Bench 4.0 SWE Atlas QnA We also ran a blind human evaluation with Surge AI on coding quality: professional annotators rated model outputs on a 1–5 scale, with model identities hidden. ML4 Preview ranked second of five models (3.74), ahead of Kimi K3 (3.59), GLM-5.3 (3.60) and GLM-5.2 (3.40), and behind only Claude Opus 5 (4.22). Agentic Workflows ML4 runs general-purpose agents that gather information, use tools, and produce finished deliverables across complex workflows. On AutomationBench — 657 business workflows across apps like Gmail, Google Sheets, Slack, and Salesforce — it scores 59.9%, ahead of Kimi K3, MiMo-V2.6-Pro, and DeepSeek V4 Pro. It's just as strong on the professional deliverables that knowledge work actually produces: spreadsheets, slides, and PDFs. On AA-Briefcase, which evaluates long-horizon knowledge work, it reaches 1,393 Elo, ahead of DeepSeek V4 Pro. AA - AutomationBench AA-Briefcase Multimodal ML4 is a step change in the ability of our models to understand images. It reasons powerfully across complex documents, charts, and natural images, and brings vision to the industries where perception is critical such as engineering, manufacturing, and earth observation. The model can further combine visual grounding with agentic capabilities: from inspecting gigapixel satellite imagery — helping disaster-response teams act when time counts — to analyzing engineering-drawings — zooming in, inspecting, and verifying until the answer is exact. In our demos above, ML4 grounds dense natural scenes, verifies mechanical parts in technical drawings, retrieves evidence from PDFs, and scans massive geospatial images for the hardest-to-find objects. On visual grounding particularly, we find ML4 to be one of the most capable models we tested, for instance surpassing GPT-6-Astra on Dense 200 (42% vs 41%). Dense 200 ChartQA Pro GDP.pdf Science and Math ML4 brings strong scientific capabilities, built by combining AI-driven methods with our researchers' expertise in mathematics, physics, and chemistry. It's highly proficient at agentic coding for scientific tasks such as data analysis, modeling, and simulating physical reality, which lets researchers focus on the questions rather than the plumbing. In benchmarks, ML4 is state of the art on SciCode-Verified among open-weight models. In practice, it can generate a full Hartree–Fock simulation in one shot — a complex, multi-step chemistry task built from a series of advanced routines. ML4's math is stronger too, in both formal reasoning and applied mathematics. In our human evaluations it reasons more precisely and with more structure than GLM-5.3, and it can sustain long, domain-specific applied-mathematics tasks, including work relevant to frontier theoretical physics. Together, these capabilities make ML4 a strong research assistant across the full technical workflow — from the first question to the final result. SciCode-Verified tests the capabilities of models to implement complex scientific workflows in code for domains such as physics, mathematics, material science and biology. Internal eval on STEM tasks (math and physics) of ML4 against GLM5.3 Knowledge Work ML4 is our most capable model for the real-world tasks which professionals handle every day. It can create, edit and fix complex spreadsheets and documents, showing exemplary performance on both legal and financial benchmarks. Notably, we evaluated ML4 through third party evaluators ( vals.ai ) on representative tasks for both legal and financial tasks, finding the model exceeds GPT-6-Astra in both cases. On HarveyAI’s Legal Agent benchmark, ML4 outperforms all open-source models. Finance Agent v2 Finch (FinWorkBench) Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark FinWorkBench tests model capabilities at creating/editing spreadsheets on real life Finance and Accounting use cases. Financial analysis demands precision and the ability to synthesize information from multiple sources, a process that remains time-consuming at many financial institutions today. In this demo, ML4 compared to other top OSS models take on the same multistep corporate finance challenge, searching through public company filings and financial reports, such as those available via EDGAR and equivalent European databases. An animated semantic map traces each model's journey toward a solution, highlighting every document retrieved along the way. Each track's position reflects the evidence gathered, the results of calculations, and the questions that remain unresolved. Viewers can follow how the investigations unfold and compare the distinct paths each model takes before arriving at its final answer. Model Safety B3 Attack Resistance Cyber Refusal Rate KORABench ML4 has saturated our benchmarks on robustness to indirect prompt injections, putting it at the frontier of OSS models (compared to GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, Kimi-K2.6, Kimi-K3, DS-V4-Pro-0813). On Lakera’s public B3 AI Security Benchmark , ML4 resists 93.3% of attacks – we see no higher scores among competitors. ML4 also engages more responsibly with users than any of our previous models. We highlight our results on the KORA Benchmark , where ML4 again sits at our highest measured score among OSS models (1.691, with 2 being the maximum denoted as “ Exemplary ”). Of particular relevance is the model’s propensity to refuse malicious requests regarding cybersecurity. Despite strong performance on Cyber benchmarks, the average refusal rate of the model on cyber prompts from JailbreakBench , StrongREJECT , and AgentHarm is higher than all OSS models. Human Evaluation We ran an internal evaluation in which expert annotators across coding, computer-aided design (CAD), finance, mathematics and physics compared Mistral Large 4 with GLM-5.3. ML4 was preferred in CAD and STEM, while performing on par or close to GLM-5.3 in finance and coding. extra.candidate_title: Codex CLI installs a persistent, self-updating background daemon by default
extra.source_text: CLI: make daemon_auto_start opt-in — a persistent, self-updating background daemon shouldn't be the default #48195 New issue Copy link New issue Copy link Open Open CLI: make daemon_auto_start opt-in — a persistent, self-updating background daemon shouldn't be the default #48195 Copy link Labels CLI Issues related to the Codex CLI Issues related to the Codex CLI app-server Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces Issues involving app server protocol or interfaces enhancement New feature or request New feature or request Description Yihua-Liu-1997 opened on Sep 25, 2026 Issue body actions What variant of Codex are you using? CLI — 0.157.0, installed via npm install -g @openai/codex , Linux (WSL2) What feature would you like to see? Please make daemon_auto_start opt-in (default false ) for the CLI , or at least ask once before turning it on. Since 0.157.0, just opening an interactive codex session: Starts a persistent background daemon ( codex app-server --managed-daemon ). It runs in its own session with no TTY and keeps running after every Codex window is closed (reparented to PID 1) until codex app-server daemon stop or a reboot. Copies the whole platform package (~374 MB: codex , codex-code-mode-host , bundled bwrap / zsh / rg ) into ~/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/releases/<version>/ — byte-identical to what npm had just installed — and runs the daemon from that copy. From then on the backend's version is decoupled from the CLI version I installed with my package manager. Starts a detached updater ( codex app-server daemon pid-update-loop ) that checks for updates 5 minutes after start and then hourly, downloads new releases and restarts the backend (which can kill active turns, see app-server daemon: auto-update force-kills active turns after a 60s drain budget, and cannot be disabled #40969 ). Pins the environment of whichever session happened to start it. I launch Codex through a wrapper that sets HTTPS_PROXY per invocation; the daemon keeps the first session's proxy variables and its outbound connections go through that proxy, whatever later sessions are launched with. Hooks in --remote mode receive the daemon's cwd, not the session's #42457 and Hooks spawned by the app-server daemon cannot identify the client terminal, breaking terminal-targeting hooks #37537 (daemon cwd / terminal instead of the session's) look like the same root cause. For a CLI, the least surprising default is that the backend lives and dies with the window, runs the binary I installed, and doesn't update itself in the background. A shared, self-updating daemon makes sense for Remote Control / the desktop app, so it would be fine to enable it there, or when the user explicitly runs codex app-server daemon start / bootstrap . If it stays on by default, please at least: exit an auto-started daemon when its last client disconnects; not copy/self-update when the CLI was installed by a package manager (npm/brew/pacman) — run the installed binary instead ( Support externally managed app-server daemon executables #41188 , npm update leaves app-server on old version, but daemon update/restart refuse recovery #46468 , Codex 0.157.0 no longer starts with the Arch Linux package unless --no-daemon is used #48050 ). Additional information Bug found while turning it off: codex app-server daemon stop stops the app-server but leaves the pid-update-loop updater running (still alive 70 s later, had to kill it manually). Workaround I'm using: codex features disable daemon_auto_start codex app-server daemon stop pkill -f ' app-server daemon pid-update-loop ' # not stopped by `daemon stop` rm -rf ~ /.codex/packages/app-server-daemon With the flag off, a new TUI session no longer spawns a daemon. extra.description: An agent skill for creating detailed, interactive isometric illustrations of real-world machines and complex systems. Generates polished SVGs with optional WebGL shaders and 3D effects.
extra.source_text:
An agent skill for creating detailed, interactive isometric illustrations of real-world machines and complex systems. Generates polished SVGs with optional WebGL shaders and 3D effects.

Anatomy

A Claude skill that explains an idea by building it as a real, working object.
Also runs in OpenCode and Codex.
Crafted, interactive isometric figures with many small precise parts, in SVG, WebGL and 3D.

   

Quick start · Gallery · What it makes · Install · Usage · Examples · How it works · Limits

examples/raptor-engine, light theme, firing. The engine and stand are SVG; the plume is a WebGL shader in the same isometric camera.

--- Ask Claude for a figure that explains a technical idea, and Anatomy has it invent a physical thing whose working *is* the concept. A cache key that skips work when nothing changed becomes a pin-tumbler lock that only turns when every pin matches. One GPU context serving many canvases becomes a gantry plotter whose single print head visits 16 wells. Then Claude builds that thing out of dozens of small, solid, shaded parts, puts it in a framed card with a title, a hint and a live readout, makes it move calmly under the pointer and the keyboard, and checks its own work by zooming in on every joint. Every number the figure shows comes from the same small model that moves its parts. ## Quick start ```sh npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g -a claude-code ``` Then, in Claude Code: ```text /anatomy explain how a token bucket rate limiter works, interactive ``` For OpenCode or Codex, swap the agent: `-a opencode` or `-a codex`. OpenCode takes the same `/anatomy` command; in Codex, type `$anatomy`. That's it. No API keys and nothing to `npm install`: the kit uses only Node's built-in modules. ## Gallery
raptor-engine: hover to take it apart into 11 assemblies. An audit proves that no pipe passes through anything, at rest, apart and in every frame between. ripple-tank: SVG apparatus over two WebGL layers (lamp light and caustics on the paper, reflections in the water) driven by a dispersion and optics model.
turning-dial: the 3D mode (beta). About 90 parts are re-projected and re-shaded every frame as you drag the dial. dial-indicator: the smallest example, about 300 lines. Hover to slide the carriage; the needle reads each block.
Every screenshot is the light theme of a page in [`examples/`](examples), captured with the skill's own [`scripts/capture.mjs`](scripts/capture.mjs) and [`scripts/drive.mjs`](scripts/drive.mjs). The built pages are committed: open any `.html` in `examples/` to try it. ## What it makes Three kinds of figure. All three share one kit, one camera and one set of craft rules. | Kind | What it is | Example | |---|---|---| | **SVG** | The core. Solid isometric parts with four-tone shading, painted back to front, in a card with a live readout and eased motion. It ships as a standalone HTML page, a lone `.svg` file with its styles embedded, or React/Next.js components. | `dial-indicator`, `desk-computer`, `arcade-cabinet`, `test-rig` | | **SVG + WebGL** | For what lines can't draw: fire, exhaust, water, caustics, lamp light, glow, steam. The shader runs in a canvas between a back and a front SVG, in the figure's own isometric camera, so it sits inside the drawing. extra.source_text:
Eleven free Claude skills that test a business before you launch it: a board trained on Hormozi, Thiel and Jobs, a marketing director, a CFO, and a consumer panel of 100 buyer agents. Free, MIT.

# The Founder skill

Eleven Claude skills that test a business before you launch it. Free, MIT, no
signup, no API key, nothing to connect.

`skills/founder-board` `skills/founder-marketing` `skills/founder-cfo`
`skills/founder-consumer` `skills/founder-launch` `skills/founder-pricing`
`skills/founder-offer` `skills/founder-competitors` `skills/founder-brand`
`skills/founder-ops` `skills/founder-plan`

One of them is your board of directors, trained on the frameworks of Alex
Hormozi, Peter Thiel and Steve Jobs. One is your marketing director. One is your
CFO and finds your real profit margins. And one is the consumer panel: it spins
up 100 buyer agents trained on your target customer and runs your business
through 100 buyer scenarios.

So you know how to launch, how to market and how to actually make money, before
you spend thousands of dollars finding out the hard way.

## Install

Paste this repo link into Claude and say `install skill`:

```
https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/founder-skill

install skill
```

Or as a plugin, in Claude Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add Jakeschincariol/founder-skill
/plugin install founder-skill@founder-skill
```

Claude Code namespaces plugin skills, so installed as a plugin they show up as
`/founder-skill:founder-board` and so on. Copy the folders instead if you want
plain `/founder-board`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/founder-skill.git
cp -r founder-skill/skills/founder-* ~/.claude/skills/
```

Project-local instead of global: copy the same folders into your repo's
`.claude/skills/`. No Claude Code at all? Paste any single `SKILL.md` at the top
of a chat and it runs as a mode. You lose the sub-agents and the Python tools,
but the method works.

The tools need Python 3.8 or newer. Nothing to pip install.

## The eleven

| command | job | what it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `/founder-board` | Board of Directors | Three board members, each a sub-agent applying one published framework (Offers, from *$100M Offers*; Monopoly, from *Zero to One*; Product, from Isaacson's *Steve Jobs*), score the idea, name what would kill it and vote. |
| `/founder-competitors` | Competitor Scout | Maps direct competitors, indirect ones and substitutes from public sources, with prices, positioning and what their customers complain about, every fact linked. |
| `/founder-consumer` | Consumer Panel | Spins up a swarm of buyer agents (100 by default) from your target customer, each with its own income, habits and objection, and tallies who buys, who doesn't and why. |
| `/founder-pricing` | Pricing Strategist | Turns the panel's price answers into an acceptable price range, sets it against competitors and your margin, and picks what to test. |
| `/founder-offer` | Offer Architect | Builds the offer stack (bonuses, guarantee, real urgency, a name) that answers the panel's objections, then re-tests it on the panel. |
| `/founder-cfo` | CFO | Unit economics: contribution per sale, the real profit margin, break-even per day, year 1 month by month, cash needed, payback, what-ifs. |
| `/founder-marketing` | Marketing Director | Positioning, the channels your buyers use, a dated 30-day launch campaign, ten hooks and the most you can pay for a customer. |
| `/founder-brand` | Brand Designer | Name candidates with the trademark, domain and handle checks to run, a voice, a promise and a brief for the look. |
| `/founder-ops` | Operations Manager | Suppliers, staffing, day-one routines, tools, the permits to check and a risk register, feeding real costs back to the CFO. |
| `/founder-launch` | Launch Lead | A cheap real-world test first, then a dated countdown, the launch-day run sheet and the first 30 days. |
| `/founder-plan` | Business Planner | Compiles everything into one business plan with a verdict computed from the numbers: Profitable, Not yet or Incomplete. |

## How to use it

Run them in this order. Each one reads what the others wrote, in a `founder/`
folder in your project.

```
board -> competitors -> consumer -> pricing -> offer -> cfo -> marketing -> brand -> ops -> launch -> plan
```

An example: a matcha café in Toronto, iced matcha lattes at $6.50 a cup. (Every
input is in the example files in this repo, so you can run the tools on it.)

1. **`/founder-board`** writes `founder/idea.md` from what you told it and puts it
   in front of three board members. Each scores it, lists the risks and votes:
   fund, fund if, or pass. The conditions become a checklist for the rest.
2. **`/founder-competitors`** maps the matcha bars and coffee shops within walking
   distance, what they charge for a latte and what their reviews complain about.
3. **`/founder-consumer`** builds the target customer (urban professionals, 24 to
   38, who buy coffee most days), deals 100 buyer cards across income, habits and
   objections, and runs one sub-agent per buyer. Back comes who buys, who passes,
   the reasons in their words ("my coffee place is closer", "$6.50 is steep for a
   drink") and what would flip a no.
4. **`/founder-pricing`** reads the panel's four price answers per buyer into a
   price range and checks $6.50 against it and against the competitors.
5. **`/founder-offer`** answers the top objections with the offer (a launch-week
   price, a loyalty card) and re-runs a quick panel to see if the buy rate moves.
6. **`/founder-cfo`** runs the unit economics. With the example numbers: each cup
   leaves $4.76 after its own costs, break-even is 186 cups a day, the profit
   margin at the planned 383 cups a day is 38%, year 1 makes $93,926 on operations
   after a slow ramp, the $25,280 startup spend is earned back in month 8, and the
   founder needs $34,092 in cash before it pays for itself.
7. **`/founder-marketing`**, **`/founder-brand`**, **`/founder-ops`** and
   **`/founder-launch`** turn it into a 30-day campaign, a name and a look, the
   suppliers and routines, and a dated launch that starts with a pop-up to test
   real buyers.
8. **`/founder-plan`** compiles `founder/business-plan.md`. Its verdict is
   computed, not written: Profitable only if every unit earns money, year 1 makes
   a profit, break-even fits capacity and enough of the panel buys.

You can also run any one on its own. `/founder-consumer --quick` on an idea you
are only thinking about is a good way to find out if you should.

## The tools

Four of them, all standard-library Python. None touch the network.

```bash
python3 skills/founder-cfo/unit_economics.py founder/numbers.json --out founder/cfo.md   # margins, break-even, year 1
python3 skills/founder-consumer/panel.py init --customer founder/customer.json --pitch founder/pitch.md
python3 skills/founder-pricing/van_westendorp.py founder/panel/answers --price 6.50       # the acceptable price range
python3 skills/founder-plan/compile.py --dir founder                                     # the plan and its verdict
```

**`unit_economics.py`** reads one JSON (example: `skills/founder-cfo/example.json`)
and reports contribution, break-even, the margin at plan, year 1 by month, cash
needed, payback and three what-ifs. Every number traces to an input; a missing
field is an error, never a guess.

**`panel.py`** deals persona cards from your target customer (same seed, same
cards), writes one brief per buyer, checks the answers and tallies them. It never
answers for a buyer.

**`van_westendorp.py`** reads four price answers per buyer (from the panel, or a
CSV from a real survey) and finds the points of marginal cheapness and
expensiveness, the optimal and the indifference price.

**`compile.py`** assembles the plan and computes the verdict.

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## Fine print

**The board applies published frameworks. It is not those people.** The three
lenses are short summaries, in our words, of ideas from *$100M Offers* by Alex
Hormozi, *Zero to One* by Peter Thiel with Blake Masters, and Walter Isaacson's
biography of Steve Jobs. The board never speaks as them, quotes them or claims
they endorse anything. This project is not affiliated with any of them.

**The consumer panel is simulated buyers, not customers.** It is a fast, cheap way
to find objections, segments and wording before you spend. It is not a forecast:
language models lean agreeable, so read the buy rate as an upper bound, and
confirm the big calls with real people. `/founder-launch` starts with exactly that
test. Panel answers are research; never use them as testimonials.

**The numbers are only as good as the inputs.** The CFO marks every estimate as an
estimate and asks for real quotes. Check costs with suppliers and the structure,
payroll and tax with an accountant.

**Research uses public sources, with links.** No invented competitors, prices,
reviews or quotes. No scraping against a site's terms.

**Not financial, legal or tax advice.** Permits, trademarks and claims depend on
where you are. The skills tell you what to check and where; a professional
confirms it.

## Files

```
skills/founder-board/        SKILL.md, lenses.md
skills/founder-competitors/  SKILL.md
skills/founder-consumer/     SKILL.md, panel.py, customer.example.json, pitch.example.md
skills/founder-pricing/      SKILL.md, van_westendorp.py
skills/founder-offer/        SKILL.md
skills/founder-cfo/          SKILL.md, unit_economics.py, example.json
skills/founder-marketing/    SKILL.md
skills/founder-brand/        SKILL.md
skills/founder-ops/          SKILL.md
skills/founder-launch/       SKILL.md
skills/founder-plan/         SKILL.md, compile.py
tests/                       the tests for every tool
```

Your own files live in `founder/` in your project. The skills read each other's.

## Credit

Made by Jake Schincariol, [opusjake.ai](https://opusjake.ai). Siblings:
[Arena](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/arena-skill),
[Replica](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/replica-skill),
[X](https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/x-agent-skill),

An agent skill that builds award-caliber websites from one line
# /awwwards **An agent skill that builds award-caliber websites from one line.**

[Demo](#demo) · [Install](#install) · [Usage](#usage) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [Limits](#limits)
``` > make me a portfolio, my name is Julio ``` That's the whole brief. The agent works as creative director, designer and creative developer in one, then hands back a site it has already checked in a real browser. ## Quick start ```bash npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g # optional: interactive isometric explainer figures npx skills add juliobsz/skills -g ``` Open a **new** agent session, then type `/awwwards` or just ask for a website. ## Demo [![Watch the demo on YouTube](https://img.youtube.com/vi/BEcQoDs16IE/maxresdefault.jpg)](https://youtu.be/BEcQoDs16IE) Click on the thumbnail to watch the demo on YouTube ## Install Install with the [skills CLI](https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills). It runs through `npx`, so there's nothing to install first, and it detects your agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Copilot and more) and lets you pick. ```bash npx skills add juliobsz/skills -g ``` | Command | Result | |---|---| | `npx skills add juliobsz/skills -g -a claude-code` | Claude Code only (use `codex`, `cursor`… for others) | | `npx skills add juliobsz/skills` | This project only, instead of your user folder | | `npx skills add juliobsz/skills -g --copy` | Copy the files instead of linking them | | `npx skills update -g` | Update to the latest version | | `npx skills remove awwwards -g` | Uninstall | The CLI collects anonymous usage data. Set `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` to turn it off.
Claude Code plugin If you prefer Claude Code's plugin system, which updates the skill for you: ``` /plugin install awwwards --marketplace juliobsz/skills ``` On Claude Code before 2.1.275, run `/plugin marketplace add juliobsz/skills` and then `/plugin install awwwards@juliobsz`. The skill then runs as `/awwwards:awwwards`. Use the plugin or the skills CLI, not both, or the skill shows up twice.
Manual install Copy the `awwwards/` folder into your agent's skills directory, for example `~/.claude/skills/awwwards`. Any agent that reads `SKILL.md` skills can use it.
### Works with /anatomy [/anatomy](https://github.com/wheresryan22/anatomy) by wheresryan22 is an open-source skill for detailed, interactive isometric figures that explain an idea as a real physical object. Install it next to `/awwwards` and the site can get one "how it works" section built as a real explainer figure, styled to the site's palette and grid. ```bash npx skills add wheresryan22/anatomy -g ``` It's optional. Without it, `/awwwards` builds that section another way, and tells you at the end when a figure would have helped. ### Requirements - **Node 22.20+** for the skills CLI. The helper scripts need Node 20+. - **Playwright** in the site's project for screenshots and the OG image, and **axe-core** for the accessibility pass. The skill installs both as dev dependencies when it needs them, and uses a Chromium you already have when it can. - **A model that can read images**, so the QA loop can look at its own screenshots. - **A Vercel, Netlify or Cloudflare account** only if you want it to deploy.
Troubleshooting - **`/awwwards` isn't found.** Start a new session; agents read their skills folder at startup. Then run `npx skills list -g` to see where it was installed. - **It shows up twice.** You installed it two ways (for example the skills CLI and the plugin). Remove one with `npx skills remove awwwards -g` or `/plugin uninstall awwwards@juliobsz`. - **Installed into the wrong agent.** Name the target with `-a`, for example `-a codex`. - **Screenshots fail with "Playwright not found".** Run `npm i -D playwright` in the site's project. If it reports no Chromium, run `npx playwright install chromium` once.
## Why Ask an agent for "a portfolio" and you get the same site everyone gets: purple gradient, three cards, "elevate your brand". This skill replaces that default with a process. - **A concept that belongs to you.** Three ideas from different territories (your name, your craft, your place), scored on originality and fit. - **A real design system.** Palette by role, curated free fonts, grid and motion language, written to `DESIGN.md` and tested against a "genericness check". - **Motion with intent.** GSAP, Lenis and WebGL (OGL) where they earn their place, with one signature moment and everything else quiet. - **Real copy.** No lorem ipsum, fake awards or invented metrics. Anything made up is marked as a placeholder and listed at the end. - **Verified, not assumed.** A production build, a crawling audit and real-browser screenshots on desktop, mobile and reduced motion, scored against a rubric until every category hits 8/10. Its quality bar is the work that wins [Awwwards](https://www.awwwards.com) Site of the Day. The site doesn't need to be submitted anywhere; it just has to be that good. ## Usage Ask in one line and let the agent decide. It writes its assumptions down instead of running a questionnaire. ``` make me a portfolio, my name is Ana a site for my architecture studio in Lisbon, we do small houses launch page for a mechanical keyboard called Kestrel, it should feel insane redesign this landing page so it could win site of the day ``` Better input gives a better site. Your real name, what you do, where you are and two or three real projects let the concept come from your story instead of a placeholder. ## How it works | Phase | What happens | |---|---| | **Brief** | Infers who it's for, the audience and the site's job. Missing facts become written assumptions | | **Concept** | Three concepts from different territories (your name, your craft's materials, your place, how you work, a formal system), scored on originality and fit. The winner becomes a one-line idea with a signature moment | | **Art direction** | Palette by role, type pairing from a curated free-font library, grid, rhythm and motion language, all written to `DESIGN.md`. Then a "genericness test" kills anything an average model would have produced | | **Build** | Semantic HTML that looks finished with motion off. Then reveals, page transitions, a loader that tracks real loading, and the signature moment | | **QA loop** | Production build, a crawling audit (SEO, metadata, accessibility, weight, placeholder copy, AI-copy tells) and real-browser screenshots on desktop, mobile, reduced motion and mid-transition. It also measures LCP and CLS on a throttled phone, runs axe and tabs through every page. The agent reads every frame, a fresh critic subagent that never saw the plan scores the site against the rubric, and the agent fixes things until every category hits 8/10 | | **Ship** | OG image, favicon, sitemap, robots, then deploy to Vercel, Netlify or Cloudflare (only after you confirm) | ### Stack - **Next.js** (App Router) by default, and for anything with app features. - **Astro** for content-only showcases where motion is the product: about 75 KB of JS against about 250 KB. - **Your stack** when you run it inside an existing project. All three use [GSAP](https://gsap.com) (every plugin is free now), [Lenis](https://lenis.dev) for smooth scroll and [OGL](https://github.com/oframe/ogl) for WebGL. The motion engine is framework-agnostic TypeScript, shipped as documented code instead of a template: it runs on one clock, reverts every effect on navigation, runs transitions in parallel with the next page loading, and keeps content visible without JavaScript or with reduced motion. ### Principles it won't break - One idea, one signature moment, everything else quiet. - Every frame works as a still poster before any motion is added. - The native cursor stays. Reduced motion gets a complete, calm site. Phones get a composed layout, not a shrunken one. - No fake awards, logos or metrics. No lorem ipsum. No em dashes or "elevate your brand" copy. - No purple gradients, glassmorphism or three-card grids unless the concept truly calls for them. ## Limits - **It takes a while.** A full run is concept, design system, build and several rounds of screenshots and fixes. Expect a long session and heavy token use, not a quick snippet. - **Results depend on the model.** It was built and tested with Claude Code and Codex. The concept and the visual QA are only as good as the model doing them. - **Content is yours to finish.** Without real projects, photos and copy, the site ships with clearly marked placeholders that you replace. - **8/10 is its own score.** The rubric keeps it honest, but you're the final judge. ## Standalone scripts The helpers in `awwwards/scripts/` work on any site, so you can use them on their own: ```bash node ~/.claude/skills/awwwards/scripts/audit.mjs https://your-site.com/ node ~/.claude/skills/awwwards/scripts/shoot.mjs https://your-site.com/ --crawl --nav ``` | Script | Does | |---|---| | `audit.mjs` | Crawl a build: SEO, a11y, weight, placeholders, AI-copy tells | | `shoot.mjs` | Screenshots of every page type: LCP/CLS on a throttled phone, FPS, overflow, tap targets, axe, keyboard focus, rest/hover pairs per pointer target, idle motion, transitions (needs Playwright; axe-core optional) | | `og.mjs` | Render the OG image from the live hero (needs Playwright) | | `font.mjs` | Self-host Fontshare / Google fonts (CSS or `next/font` output) | | `photos.mjs` | Contact sheets of free photos for marked placeholders | | `serve.mjs` | Static server for build output |

--- ## 截图 · Screenshots

--- ## 中文 **Win顺** 是 Windows 上免费开源的快速搜索启动器：连按两下 Ctrl 弹出搜索框，边打字边出结果。按文件名或拼音秒找文件，搜 Word、Excel、PDF 里的文字，打开应用和系统设置，还有剪贴板历史、对话框搜索、任务栏搜索框、插件和给 AI 用的 MCP 搜索。 它直接读 NTFS 主文件表（MFT）建索引，三百多万个文件几秒建好，增删改名实时跟上，**不用装 Everything**。不需要账号，不上传数据。界面有简体中文和英文。 ### 功能 #### 🔍 文件搜索 - **双击 Ctrl** 打开，再按一次或 `Esc` 关闭；三百多万个文件里搜一次只要几毫秒。 - **拼音和首字母**：`ndbg` → 年度报告，`baog` → 报告；多音字按常用读音。打错了同音字（年度报高）找不到时，自动按读音再找一遍。 - **搜整台电脑**：所有本地磁盘，U 盘可选（没收录的 U 盘插着时，列表末尾会提示你顺手搜一下它）；**NAS、内网共享文件夹（SMB）** 也能加进来一起搜，服务器关机时收录过的照样能搜到。 - **排序懂你**：自己的文件在前，系统目录、`node_modules` 在后，名字完全一样的最前。每行显示修改日期，`Ctrl+S` 在最匹配、最新、最早之间切换。不输入时列出最近打开或最近修改的文件。 - **数字键直达**：结果的图标上标着序号，`Ctrl+1`～`Ctrl+9` 打开第几行（也可改成 `Alt`）。 - **按类型找**：选中 **文件** 后，下面一排是文件夹、文档、图片、视频、压缩包等类型，`Tab` 依次切换；点 `+` 或在设置里自己加类型。 - **拖出去就能用**：结果直接拖进微信、邮件、资源管理器。 - **实时更新**：读 USN 变更日志，改名、新建、删除马上搜得到；拔 U 盘不会提示“设备正在使用”。 | 搜索语法 | 含义 | |---|---| | `报告 2024` | 每个词都要有（空格分隔，顺序不限）；也可以在所在文件夹的名字里 | | `ndbg`、`niandubaogao` | 拼音全拼、首字母，可以混用 | | `"年度 报告"` | 引号内作为整体 | | `!草稿`、`!node_modules\` | 排除文件名、排除文件夹 | | `*.pdf`、`报告?.docx` | 通配符 | | `ext:pdf,docx` | 只要这些扩展名 | | `项目\readme` | 在名字含“项目”的文件夹下 | | `tools/out/`、`D:\My Files\` | 路径直达：回车进去，列出里面的内容 | #### 📄 文件内容全文搜索 - 切到 **内容** 范围，搜文件里的文字，结果显示命中的那一行。 - **能搜的文件**： - 纯文本：txt、md、log、csv、json、代码等； - 文档：**Word、Excel、PowerPoint、PDF、WPS**，结果里显示第几页、第几张幻灯片或哪个表的第几行。 - **怎么找**：可以写多个词、用引号找整个短语，结果按相关度排。 - **编码和速度**：自动识别 UTF-8、UTF-16、GBK 编码；有内容索引，几十万个文件也很快。超过大小上限的、系统目录里的、类型没列出的文件默认不搜，搜完会告诉你各有几个，点一下就临时把它们也搜了。 - **安全**：文档由一个权限受限的独立进程读取。 #### 🚀 应用和系统设置 - **应用**：开始菜单里的所有应用都能搜，含 Microsoft Store 应用。名称、拼音、首字母（`vsc`）、程序名（`winword`）都行；`Ctrl+Shift+Enter` 以管理员身份运行。 - **系统设置**：约 1200 个 Windows 设置页和控制面板项。`shipeiqi`、“网卡”、`ncpa.cpl` 都能打开网络连接；另外补了组策略、磁盘管理、hosts、AppData 等开始菜单里没有的。 #### 🌐 网页搜索 · ⭐ 收藏夹 · 🧩 插件 - **网页搜索**：`baidu 天气`、`zhihu 显卡`、`jingdong 键盘`，关键词加空格就在那个网站上搜。 - 自带百度、必应、B 站、知乎、微博、抖音、小红书、淘宝、京东、翻译。 - 可以用 `%s` 网址添加自己的网站，图标、列表都能导入导出。 - **收藏夹**： - 右键“加入收藏夹”，不打字时排在最前； - 起个关键词，一打就开； - 收藏的文件夹按 `Tab` 进去接着搜。 - **插件**： - 随包的小工具：`= 1+2*3` 计算器、`12 inch to cm` 单位换算、`#ff8800` 颜色，还有时间戳、UUID、Base64、哈希； - `kill` 结束进程，`bm` 搜浏览器书签，`tr` 翻译； - 自己写插件：零代码的 `plugin.json`、任意语言的脚本或常驻进程都行，附 Python / PowerShell / C++ SDK； - 插件以普通权限、限内存运行。见 [docs/plugins.md](docs/plugins.md)。 #### 📂 “打开”“另存为”对话框 - **对话框旁的搜索框**：输入文件夹或文件名（拼音也行），回车，对话框直接转过去；网页上传文件、WPS 的对话框也认。 - **`Ctrl+G`**：转到资源管理器、Total Commander 或 Directory Opus 正在显示的文件夹，和 Listary 的同名快捷键一样。 - **不输入时**：列出打开着的文件夹、刚复制的路径、收藏和最近用过的文件夹。 - **自动转过去**：可以设成对话框一出现就转到文件管理器的文件夹，或者先停在上次的位置，从文件管理器切回来时再转。 #### 📋 剪贴板历史（代替 Win+V） - **记什么**：复制过的文字、图片、文件都记下来。 - **怎么打开**：`Win+V` 或自设的快捷键；开在输入光标旁，不抢焦点。 - **怎么粘贴**：双击或 `Enter` 粘贴，`Shift+Enter` 粘贴为纯文本，`Alt+1`～`9` 直接粘贴第几条（序号标在图标上）。 - **能搜**：拼音搜索，`@wx` 只看微信里复制的；**图片里的字也能搜**（Windows 自带的文字识别 OCR，在本机，不联网）。 - **预览**：全文、大图、颜色值的 HEX / RGB / HSL。 - **拖出图片**：按住一张图片拖到文件夹里，就存成 PNG 文件。 - **整理**：固定、分组、多选按顺序合并粘贴，钉住后可以一条接一条地往表格里填。 - **隐私**：密码管理器复制的密码不记录，历史只存在本机。 #### 🔎 任务栏搜索框（代替 Windows 搜索） - 在 Windows 11 任务栏上放 Win顺 自己的搜索框（Windows 10 是固定一个按钮），结果从任务栏上方滑出。 - 可以像 Windows 自带的搜索框一样放在开始按钮右边，图标往右让出位置（设置里打开，默认关）。 - 可以接管 `Win+S`，开始菜单里打字也用 Win顺 搜。 #### 🤖 AI 助手（MCP） - **能做什么**：Win顺 是一个 MCP 服务器，AI 能用它搜文件名、文件内容和最近修改的文件。 - **怎么连**：Claude Desktop、Claude Code、Cursor、VS Code 在设置里一键连接。 - **安全**： - 默认只读，只看得到 AI 客户端自己有权限看的文件； - 可以设不让 AI 看到的文件夹； - 每次调用都有记录。 #### 🎨 外观和设置 - **外观**：浅色、深色跟随系统，Windows 11 云母（Mica）效果和圆角；图标在 150% 缩放下也清晰。 - **设置**：可以搜索（`Ctrl+F`，`kjj` 找到“快捷键”），改了立即生效。 - **更新**：有新版本时在托盘提醒，Win顺 不会自己下载、替换程序文件。 | 按键 | 作用 | |---|---| | 双击 `Ctrl` | 打开 / 关闭搜索框（可另设组合键，如 `Alt+Space`） | | `Enter` / `Ctrl+Enter` / `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` | 打开 / 打开所在文件夹 / 以管理员身份运行 | | `Ctrl+C` / `Ctrl+Shift+C` | 复制文件 / 复制路径 | | `Ctrl+1`～`Ctrl+9` | 打开第几行（图标上的数字） | | `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` | 切换范围：全部 / 文件 / 内容；在 **文件** 里 `Tab` 切换类型 | | `Ctrl+S` | 最匹配 → 最新在前 → 最早在前 | | `Ctrl+G`（对话框里） | 转到文件管理器正在显示的文件夹 | | `Win+V` / `Win+S`（设置里打开后） | 剪贴板历史 / 任务栏上方的搜索框 | ### 下载安装 1. 到 [Releases 页面](https://github.com/LingCore/WinShun/releases/latest) 下载 `WinShun-版本号-x64-setup.exe`，双击安装。Windows 提示“已保护你的电脑”时，点 **更多信息 → 仍要运行**（还没有代码签名证书）。 2. 装完托盘里出现 Win顺 的图标，索引几秒就建好。连按两下 Ctrl 开始搜索。 3. 升级时运行新的安装程序，设置和索引都保留。卸载在 Windows 的“设置 → 应用”里。 不想安装的话，下载 `WinShun-版本号-x64-portable.zip`，解压到任意文件夹，运行里面的 `WinShun.exe` 就行。设置和索引和安装版放在同一个地方（`%APPDATA%\WinShun`、`%LOCALAPPDATA%\WinShun`），不在解压的文件夹里；升级时用新版的文件夹换掉旧的。 系统要求：Windows 10 或 11，64 位。 ### 为什么需要管理员权限 - **为什么要**：读 NTFS 主文件表（MFT）和 USN 变更日志，才能几秒建好索引、实时跟上改动。开机自启用的是最高权限的计划任务，所以开机不弹 UAC。 - **打开的东西仍是普通权限**：从 Win顺 打开的文件和应用都以普通权限运行，只有 `Ctrl+Shift+Enter` 才以管理员身份运行。 ### 常见问题 **和 Everything、Listary 有什么区别？** Win顺 自己建索引，不用装 Everything。文件名、拼音、应用和文件内容在一个框里搜，针对中文做了优化。对话框里有和 Listary 一样的 `Ctrl+G` 和搜索框，但不嵌进资源管理器窗口。 **双击 Ctrl 和别的软件冲突？** Listary、PowerToys 的“查找鼠标”默认也用双击 Ctrl，关掉其中一边就行。也可以在 Win顺 里改用别的组合键。游戏全屏、藏起鼠标时，Win顺 默认不响应双击 Ctrl。 **AutoHotkey 改的键在 Win顺 里不起作用？** Win顺 以管理员身份运行，Windows 不让普通权限的程序拦截发给它的按键。用 AutoHotkey 的 UI Access 模式，或以管理员身份运行脚本。 **占多少内存？索引能不放 C 盘吗？** - **内存**：每 100 万个文件约 30 MB，用着的时候整个程序一般 120～140 MB；不用它一分钟后，任务管理器里降到十几 MB。 - **索引位置**：在设置 → 高级 → 索引位置里，可以移到其他内置硬盘。 **收费吗？会上传数据吗？** 完全免费，MIT 开源。只在两种时候联网：到 GitHub 检查新版本（可以关掉），第一次显示某个网页搜索时取一次那个网站的图标。索引和历史只存在本机（`%LOCALAPPDATA%\WinShun`）。 ### 反馈 遇到问题或有建议，欢迎在 [Issues](https://github.com/LingCore/WinShun/issues) 里提出。 ### 从源码编译 需要 Visual Studio 2022（“使用 C++ 的桌面开发”）、Qt 6.8 或更新版本（推荐 6.12，MSVC 2022 64 位套件）、CMake 3.25+ 和 Ninja。 ```powershell ./scripts/build.ps1 # 编译 + 运行单元测试 ./scripts/build.ps1 -QtDir C:\Qt\6.12.0\msvc2022_64 # 指定 Qt（默认用 QTDIR 或 C:\Qt 下最新的版本） ./scripts/build.ps1 -Deploy # 生成可分发的文件夹 dist\WinShun ./scripts/release.ps1 # 打包安装程序和 SHA256SUMS.txt（需要 Inno Setup 6.5+）；加 -Publish 发布到 GitHub ``` 也可以用 Qt Creator 或 VS Code（CMake Tools）打开，预设见 `CMakePresets.json`。源码结构和设计见 [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md)，踩过的坑见 [docs/pitfalls.md](docs/pitfalls.md)。 --- ## English **WinShun** (Win顺, "Windows made smooth") is a free, open-source search launcher for Windows. Press Ctrl twice and a search bar pops up, with results as you type: - find files and folders by name or by pinyin; - search the text inside Word, Excel and PDF files; - launch apps and open Windows settings. It also brings a clipboard history, a search bar for file dialogs, a taskbar search box, plugins and an MCP server for AI assistants. It reads the NTFS master file table (MFT) directly, indexing three million files in a few seconds and following every change live: **no Everything install needed**. It needs no account and uploads nothing. The interface comes in English and Simplified Chinese. Screenshots: [above](#screenshots). ### Features

# MiniCPM-V 4.7 [On-device results](#on-device-capability-and-efficiency) · [Evaluation](#evaluation) · [Examples](#examples) · [Usage](#usages) · [Model weights](#model-weights) **MiniCPM-V 4.7** is the latest model in the MiniCPM-V series, available in a **35B-A3B** variant, with **35B-A3B being the first MoE model in the MiniCPM-V series**. It builds on the family's single-image, multi-image, and video understanding capabilities, combining stronger foundation capabilities with efficient visual encoding and on-device inference. Notable features of MiniCPM-V 4.7 include: - 📱 **The First Open-Source MoE Model with Lossless, Smooth On-Device Inference.** With our [**Lookahead Expert Scheduling (LES)**](https://github.com/tc-mb/llama.cpp-omni/blob/master/docs/les/lookahead-expert-scheduling.md) technique introduced alongside MiniCPM-V 4.7, combined with fine-grained layer-wise quantization and DSpark speculative sampling integration, MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B-A3B becomes the **first open-source MoE model to run smoothly on-device without compromising performance**, achieving a decoding speed of **13+ tokens/s with just 3 GB of memory on iPhone 17 Pro Max**. - 🔥 **A New Pareto Frontier in Performance and Efficiency.** As model capabilities continue to advance, inference efficiency has become an important measure of a model's value. On resource-constrained devices, delivering the strongest possible capabilities within a limited resource budget calls for higher capability density. The **35B-A3B** variant of MiniCPM-V 4.7 advances the performance–efficiency Pareto frontier for MLLMs. In Instruct mode, 35B-A3B **achieves a higher overall score in less inference time than Qwen3.6 35B-A3B**. - 🚀 **Efficient Architecture.** Based on the intra-ViT early compression technique from [LLaVA-UHD v4](https://github.com/THUMAI-Lab/LLaVA-UHD-v4), MiniCPM-V 4.7 compresses visual tokens early within the vision encoder, reducing computation in subsequent encoder layers. It also supports **mixed 4x/16x visual token compression**, allowing developers to balance visual detail and inference cost across tasks. - 💻 **Broad Platform and Chip Support.** MiniCPM-V 4.7 supports **iOS, Android, and HarmonyOS**, together with open-source on-device deployment support. It also provides **day-0 support for chip platforms from Rockchip, Houmo, Intel, AMD, and Arm**, extending deployment options across mobile and local computing devices. - 🛠️ **Developer Friendly.** MiniCPM-V 4.7 supports [inference frameworks](https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM-o/blob/main/docs/deployment_en.md#supported-inference-and-training-frameworks-and-api) including SGLang, vLLM, llama.cpp, and Ollama, along with [fine-tuning frameworks](https://github.com/OpenBMB/MiniCPM-o/blob/main/docs/deployment_en.md#supported-inference-and-training-frameworks-and-api) including SWIFT and LLaMA-Factory. It provides GGUF, BNB, AWQ, and GPTQ quantized variants and adds **FP8 quantization support**. We also release **Self-Replay Fine-Tuning**, a fine-tuning approach that helps developers extend model capabilities at low cost while reducing forgetting of existing capabilities, making further customization easier. ## Get started

Model weights  ·  Inference  ·  Fine-tuning  ·  Live demo  ·  Local deployment  ·  API  ·  Cookbook

### On-Device Capability and Efficiency #### Smooth On-Device MoE Inference without compromising performance An MoE model can have far more total parameters than it activates for a single token, but its on-device storage requirements are not limited to those active parameters. Different tokens can select different experts at different layers, while device memory often cannot hold all expert weights. Without a latency constraint, weights can remain on SSD or other storage, be loaded as needed, and be released after computation. This makes large-model inference possible, but repeated loading stalls can make decoding too slow for real-time interaction. Another approach is to restrict the pool of available experts. For example, fixing an expert subset for an entire prompt can reduce loading frequency, but limits subsequent token-level routing to that subset, potentially excluding experts the model would otherwise select and reducing its capabilities. The central goal is therefore **smooth inference without compromising performance**: preserving model capability while delivering sufficient throughput under limited memory and bandwidth. MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B-A3B addresses this challenge through three complementary techniques: - [**Lookahead Expert Scheduling (LES)**](https://github.com/tc-mb/llama.cpp-omni/blob/master/docs/les/lookahead-expert-scheduling.md) uses cross-layer routing prediction to preload experts likely to be needed by the next layer. Among the experts selected by the actual router, it prioritizes those successfully prefetched and overlaps their computation with loading the remaining required experts. Predictions guide only prefetching and scheduling; computation still follows the model's original token-level routing, and required experts missed by the prediction are loaded and evaluated as usual. - **Fine-grained layer-wise quantization** reduces the storage footprint and memory traffic of expert weights while preserving model capability, making expert loading better suited to on-device memory and bandwidth constraints. - **DSpark speculative sampling integration** incorporates speculative sampling into the on-device inference process, working with expert scheduling and quantization to improve decoding efficiency. Together, these techniques make MiniCPM-V 4.7 35B-A3B the first open-source MoE model to run smoothly on-device without compromising performance, achieving **13+ tokens/s on iPhone 17 Pro Max**. **On-Device MoE Inference: Before and After Optimization**
